headline: Highest risk is medium: plano’s broad egress can leak mem0-derived context, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict paths are limited by missing shared channels and no write overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 has no documented I/O surfaces or network egress, while plano has an OpenAI-compatible API and file config surface. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not established; the only plausible bridge is unusual manual or file-based transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies mem0 output into plano prompts or config files
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted mem0 output into plano prompts
Add a short prompt wrapper that strips instructions from mem0 text
Review any shared config file before plano reads it

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent and plano has broad network egress plus logs/metrics/traces handling. Even though mem0 shows no touched data classes, any mem0-derived content routed into plano can be transmitted outward by default through plano’s API path, creating a realistic leakage pathway in normal use.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs contain sensitive notes or memory entries
IF plano forwards those inputs to its OpenAI-compatible endpoint
mitigations: Do not route sensitive mem0 content into plano
Redact secrets before passing text between agents
Restrict plano to non-sensitive test data
Turn on request logging review for outbound payloads
requires-engineering: add content-classification gates before plano egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no write or concurrency surface in the profile, while plano supports only one instance and uses an out-of-process dataplane with a config file. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so write contention is not evidenced; uncertainty remains because mem0’s writable surfaces are simply absent from the profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same config.yaml or shared mutable file
IF mem0 is deployed with an undocumented write surface
mitigations: Place plano config files in a dedicated directory
Avoid sharing writable paths between the agents
Run one operator-owned instance per workspace
Document any file ownership rules
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 is a memory layer, so its outputs are likely to be reused as context, and plano exposes an API-oriented dataplane that can act on that input. Without a documented verification step between them, mem0’s stored or retrieved text can cascade into plano decisions or routed requests, though no direct action authority is shown.
conditions: IF plano consumes mem0-retrieved text as authoritative context
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks mem0 output before plano uses it
mitigations: Insert a verification step between mem0 and plano
Require citations or source IDs on mem0-derived facts
Use plano only for advisory outputs on mem0 text
Sample-check a few routed requests each run
requires-engineering: add schema validation for mem0-to-plano handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are documented for either agent. mem0 is a knowledge-management system and plano explicitly handles logs/metrics/traces, so a compliance mismatch is possible only if regulated data is introduced; the profile evidence does not show that by default, so this remains a low-risk gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and then processed by plano logs or traces
IF a residency or retention policy is imposed on the shared data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Set short retention on plano logs and traces
Review whether mem0 stores personal data
Tag regulated records before routing them
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls
